content.title: Wrapping and Flexible Space
content.hook: A layout that looks fine with three cards may fail when the available width gets smaller.
content.context:
That is not mysterious.

The container simply has less room.

Flexbox can respond by allowing items to wrap, or by allowing items to share available space more flexibly.
goals: Understand that a row can run out of room and learn the basic roles of `flex-wrap` and `flex: 1`.

content.title: Wrapping

content.question:
A row contains six cards. The available width becomes much smaller.

With `flex-wrap: wrap`, what is the intended behavior?

options.text: Items may continue on additional rows instead of being forced to remain on one row.
The parent becomes taller by exactly 6px.
The browser removes the last card.

feedback.correct: Wrapping gives the items another row to use when the original row no longer has enough room.
feedback.incorrect: Wrapping gives the items another row to use when the original row no longer has enough room.

content.title: Flexible children

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Compose your response below, then submit to compare with the reference guide.

content.prompt:
Create three cards inside a flex container with a visible width.

First use `display: flex` without wrapping.

Then add `flex-wrap: wrap`.

Then try `flex: 1` on the cards.

Observe the difference between:

- allowing another row;
- allowing items to share the current row's space.
guidelines: State your reasoning clearly in your own words or code.
Compare your response with the reference guide after submitting.
content.sampleResponse: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.

feedback.correct: Review your explanation against the core mental model of this lesson.
feedback.incorrect: Please write a brief response (at least 10 characters) before submitting.

content.question:
Which choice best matches each goal?

**Goal A:** let items move onto another row when space runs out.

**Goal B:** let sibling items share available space.

feedback.correct: Wrapping changes how many rows the layout can use. `flex: 1` changes how the items can share available space.
feedback.incorrect: Wrapping changes how many rows the layout can use. `flex: 1` changes how the items can share available space.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Responsive layout problems often begin with available space. Wrapping changes rows; flexible sizing changes how items share a row.
**Senior habit:** Ask whether the layout needs another row or a different distribution of space.
**Mastery signal:** You can distinguish “make another row” from “share the current row better.”
